rep.angle: lead with a recent hiring push you noticed
rep.name: Dev

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Sam Whitfield. I have fifteen minutes, go ahead.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Sam, I noticed Northwind’s recent sales hiring push. May I ask two questions about ramp time to see whether this merits fifteen minutes?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Ask them. Then tell me why this is worth forty-eight thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Absolutely. With 40 reps, how long until new hires are call-ready, and what does each month below productivity cost Northwind?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: A new rep costs us about $90,000 a year fully loaded, or $7,500 a month; I don’t have a clean call-ready figure. Show me how much ramp time you can credibly cut and how that recovers $48,000.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: I wouldn’t promise a ramp reduction without your baseline. One month saved across seven hires recovers $52,500; how many hires are planned this year?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Seven hires is roughly our plan. What evidence supports cutting a full month, and can you get the price below $35,000?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: A 30-day pilot would measure readiness against your baseline; I won’t claim a month beforehand. Below $35,000 means 32 reps—which team should start?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Thirty-two reps doesn’t solve a forty-rep requirement. I need all forty at $35,000; what commitment do you need from us to get there, and what pilot metric proves at least $48,000 in annual value?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Can you do all forty at $35,000 for annual prepayment, yes or no? For the pilot, define the readiness metric and show how it supports at least 6.4 aggregate rep-months saved.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: No—annual prepayment alone won’t get forty to $35,000. Pilot success is 6.4 aggregate rep-months faster to a quote-evidenced readiness threshold versus baseline, worth $48,000.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That threshold is too vague, and 6.4 months only gets me to breakeven at your quoted price. What commitment besides prepayment gets forty seats to $35,000, and exactly what observable event marks a rep as ready?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: To reach $35,000, I’d need a three-year non-cancellable term and reference rights. Ready means three consecutive benchmark calls scoring 85%+, each score quote-cited.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Three years non-cancellable is too much risk for an unproven result. I’ll trade annual prepayment and reference rights after verified success for forty seats at $35,000, contingent on the pilot demonstrating 6.4 aggregate rep-months saved against a jointly fixed baseline and scoring rubric; can you do that?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: I understand the risk, but no. I can do $39,000 with prepayment and post-success reference rights; business-case review Thursday at 2—you, your CRO, and me?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Thirty-nine thousand is still above my ceiling; make it Thursday, November 5 at 2:00 p.m. with our VP of Sales, and bring the pilot baseline, rubric, quantified upside beyond breakeven, and a path to $35,000. Send me the business case and we'll take it from there.
